main_body: Altar drawn as a white cloth/panel with a lavender book panel and cross (rows 11-23), a gold trim band, and a purple front face with a cross (rows 26-34), standing on a grey stone step
top_band: none. The column runs white or lavender (rows 11-23), then a gold line (rows 24-25), then the purple front (rows 26-34). The only surface that could be a top is the 13-row white block, and it is a vertical panel with a face-on cross, not a foreshortened top.
evidence: Both the upper white/lavender block and the lower purple block are face-on vertical surfaces, each with its own cross. The 13-row white area is far too tall to be a foreshortened top. The gold row 24 is a 1-2px trim line and the dark row 25 is only an underline, so neither is a top surface. The grey step at rows 37-39 is a small base detail and cannot give the main body a top. This matches the red 'front elevation' guide with no visible horizontal surface, so it fails.

style.evidence: The measured facts are below both references: 25 distinct colours against 40 and 38, 13 colours per tile against 17 and 20, and 23% flat-fill coverage against 13% and 0%. The white cloth block is a large flat fill with no fold, weave or grain. The purple front has only about 3 steps with vertical stripes. Edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines carry a tint rather than the near-black sticker look, but the large flat areas leave the piece thinner than the references.
